time_expectation: Designed so that a correct solution (sequence export, Bloch simulation of about 8e3 isochromats, non-Cartesian reconstruction and checks) fits within the 60-minute session on a shared CPU without GPU.
acquisition: 2D single-slice interleaved spiral-out gradient echo at z = 0: each interleave is one slice-selective 90 deg excitation followed by one ADC during a spiral-out readout gradient in the x-y plane; the number of interleaves (1 to 36) and the spiral design are your choice
flip_angle_definition: realized on-resonance flip angle 360 deg x |integral of the RF waveform (Hz)| within 2%; every RF pulse is played with a z gradient on and no x or y gradient, RF frequency offset 0; no other RF pulses
repetition_time_definition: interval between consecutive excitation centres, identical for all interleaves (tolerance 1 us); with T1 <= 0.6 s no preparation is needed
echo_time_definition: from the excitation centre to the first ADC sample of the interleave, at which the nominal trajectory must satisfy |k| <= 1 cycle/m; tolerance 10 us
hardware_note: limits apply per axis to the exported piecewise-linear waveforms, including the transitions between the declared first/last values and the raster samples of arbitrary gradients and the boundaries between blocks

sampling_contract.adc_events: one ADC per interleave, all with the same number of samples (sample times delay + (i+0.5) x dwell), ADC window at most max_readout_duration_s
sampling_contract.k_space_rule: nominal k-space positions are the time integrals of the exported gradients (Pulseq piecewise-linear interpretation) from the excitation centre
sampling_contract.kz: kz = 0 within 0.05 cycles/m at every sample
sampling_contract.coverage: the union of the nominal sample positions of all interleaves must cover the disc |k| <= 18/fov_m: every point of the disc lies within 0.6/fov_m of some sample

gradient_delay_model: Real gradient chains lag the ADC. A measurement may be acquired with a known constant delay delta between all gradient waveforms and the ADC: the sample recorded at nominal time t has the k-space position k_nominal(t - delta). The archive key gradient_delay_s holds delta: 0 for the public measurement you simulate; the hidden measurements use nonzero values with |delta| <= 11 us, written into that key. The simulator realises the delay by shifting every ADC sampling time by -delta.
image_quality_requirement: for each hidden measurement, the magnitude image from reconstruct.py must have a normalized RMS difference (after a least-squares scale) of at most 0.10 from a reference reconstruction of the same object acquired with delta = 0

phantom.content: x_m [36], y_m [36] (x_m[18] = y_m[18] = 0), z_offsets_m [11], and 36x36 [y,x] maps density, T1_s, T2_s, B0_Hz, labels
phantom.isochromat_model: every in-plane voxel with density > 0 is a column of 11 isochromats at (x_m[ix], y_m[iy], z_offsets_m[n]) spread over -3.6 mm < z < 3.6 mm, each with density/11 and the voxel's T1 (<= 0.6 s), T2 (the only transverse decay), B0 = 0; magnetization starts at thermal equilibrium; noise-free

endpoint: complex image on the 36x36 [y,x] grid; per vial, the median magnitude over the vial voxels not touching another label divided by the same quantity for label 1
bloch_simulation: simulate the exported sequence.seq file itself with an established Bloch simulator (KomaMRI is the reference implementation; MRzero is acceptable); do not replace it with your own Bloch or EPG code

simulation_output_schema.raw_signal: complex [n_interleaves, n_samples], chronological, after ADC phase demodulation; encoding exp(-2 pi i (kx x + ky y)); an arbitrary single global receiver phase is accepted
simulation_output_schema.kxy_cycles_per_m: float [n_interleaves, n_samples, 2] nominal k-space positions from the exported sequence
simulation_output_schema.adc_times_s: float [n_interleaves, n_samples] nominal absolute sample times
simulation_output_schema.phantom_sha256: SHA256 of the phantom file used
simulation_output_schema.other_keys: allowed; passed through unchanged to the hidden archives

reconstruct_cli: python reconstruct.py --input simulation.npz --output image.npz. Standalone: helper code inside this one file, installed third-party imports allowed; it must work in a clean directory with only this file and the archive, using only the archive contents. It is rerun on archives with the same keys whose raw_signal comes from another object acquired with your sequence and whose gradient_delay_s is nonzero.

image_output_schema.image: complex [36,36] on the [y,x] grid of the phantom (row index increases with y, column with x), no flips or shifts

report_output_schema.realized_echo_time_ms: float measured from the exported sequence
report_output_schema.trajectory_design: string: how the waveform meets the gradient and slew limits on the raster
report_output_schema.signal_ratio_by_label: object mapping "2".."6" to the endpoint ratio measured on your image

grading_note: The grader reads the exported sequence back, checks limits, rasters, RF, TR, TE, readout length, kz and k-space coverage from its own integration of the waveforms, replays the file in KomaMRI on the public object and on a hidden object with delta = 0 and two hidden delays, compares your simulated signal, and reruns reconstruct.py on the delayed hidden measurements.
